log_meta.commit_policy: One git commit per logged action.
log_meta.file_layout: Single canonical JSON file; lines keyed by line_id, each holding a timestamp-ordered events array.
log_meta.tools: tools/lineage.py --write recomputes derived lineage fields and validates the log. tools/media.py reports media consumption, depletion forecasts and delivered PG. tools/ramp_model.py characterises the controller ramp from evolver_code/custom_script.py.
log_meta.validation: tools/validate_schema.py checks shape against schema/evolution_log.schema.json. tools/lineage.py checks the cross-field constraints a JSON Schema cannot express: params keys registered, event types declared, lineage acyclic and consistent, event counter correct. tools/test_media.py checks the consumption model. A file that passes the schema is well formed, not necessarily correct.

experiment.title: Modified-morbidostat laboratory evolution of E. coli for increased phloroglucinol tolerance (phase 2)
experiment.objective: Evolve increased phloroglucinol (PG) tolerance in E. coli BL21 and BL21-DE3 under a deterministic PG ramp, while controlling for media-background-specific adaptation by alternating media in a subset of lines.
experiment.backfill_policy: No retrospective backfill. Log opens with the t0 inoculation snapshot reconstructed from 2026-08-23-initial_setup.md; all subsequent actions are logged forward as they occur.

selective_agent.name: phloroglucinol
selective_agent.note: Molar mass is for the anhydrous form. If the dihydrate (CAS 6099-90-7, 162.14 g/mol) is used for stock preparation, record the form in the weighing event params so g/L->mM conversion can be corrected.

MS.note: Registered but has not contributed to the experiment as of log initialization.

design.layout: Started as 2 strains x 2 media x 2 modes x 2 replicates = 16 lines, mode confounded with eVOLVER unit. Two losses since: the 2026-08-23 flooding took the four patrick LB lines, of which two were restarted, and the vial 6 overheat at 11:50 killed one of those restarts. BL21-DE3 / LB / constant now has NO surviving line; BL21 / LB / constant has one, patrick-v05#2. M9 and switch-mode cells are untouched at 2 replicates each.

mode_definitions.constant: Line is evolved in a single, unchanging media background (LB or M9) for the duration of the run.
mode_definitions.switch: Media background is alternated between LB and M9 over the course of the run so that selection is not for media-specific traits. Switches are event-driven, not on a fixed calendar.

design.mode_unit_confound: Constant mode ran on patrick and switch mode on plankton from setup until 2026-08-26, so unit effects could not be separated from mode effects. plankton-v13 and plankton-v14 are the first switch lines founded from a constant-mode parent, which crosses that boundary in lineage but not in hardware: they still sit on plankton. The confound stands.

pg_ramp.type: deterministic increment, gated on sustained growth
pg_ramp.ceiling_note: The vial can never reach the high reservoir's concentration. Hardware forces a minimum 0.5 mL dispense from the low pump, so every cycle adds some low media; above about 4.78 g/L the best available step is negative and the ramp stalls. Attainable ceiling is ~96% of the high reservoir concentration at a 22 mL vial volume, so reaching 5 g/L in the vial would require a stronger high reservoir, not more time.
pg_ramp.bootstrap_note: With target_ramp at 0.1 g/L the low-end overshoot is gone: the smallest step the hardware can take from the floor is ~0.083 g/L from a 0.5 g/L low reservoir and ~0.093 g/L from a PG-free one, both now just under the target rather than roughly double it as they were at 0.05.
pg_ramp.minimum_cycles_note: 49 two-step cycles from 0 g/L, or 43 from the 0.5 g/L LB floor, to reach 4.7 g/L if every cycle ramped. Halved by the 2026-08-24 step-size change. Real progress is far slower because ramps are gated on growth; this is a lower bound on run length, not a forecast.
pg_ramp.dilution_trigger: raw sensor value <= setpoint (raw values fall as density rises)
pg_ramp.dispense_geometry: two steps of 5 mL each, split between the low and high pumps
open_questions: Per-vial setpoint, interval and number_consecutive_intervals are set in experiment_parameters.yaml, which has not been captured. Without them the ramp cannot be reconstructed for any line.

The vial volume the controller uses for its concentration arithmetic is unknown. The log records a 25 mL culture volume; the function default is 22 mL. If the controller assumes 22 mL while the vial truly holds 25 mL, every achieved step is about 16% smaller than intended (0.042 vs 0.050 g/L) and the controller's recorded concentrations drift high over the run.
pg_ramp.low_media_floor_interaction: Raising the LB low reservoir to 0.5 g/L changes what the ramp can do at the bottom of the range. Pure low media now carries PG, so a vial below 0.5 g/L is pushed upward even when the controller is holding: from 0 g/L the smallest achievable move is about +0.17 g/L per cycle, and the growth gate cannot prevent it. Any LB line below 0.5 g/L converges on 0.5 within roughly three dilutions regardless of how it is growing. The two restarted patrick LB lines were inoculated at 0 g/L, so their effective starting concentration is 0.5 g/L, not 0.
pg_ramp.bootstrap_branch_caveat: find_optimal_pump_volumes short-circuits below c1_min and returns the minimum hardware step, (maxdispense, maxdispense - pump_min), which always draws some high media. The c1_min derivation assumes the low reservoir is PG-free: it compares the minimum step against 'doing nothing' being a zero change, which stopped being true when LB low went to 0.5 g/L. With low = 0.5 and a vial at 0 g/L while holding, the branch produces +0.25 g/L where all-low media would have produced +0.17 g/L, so it overshoots by more than the alternative it is supposed to be avoiding. Transient — it stops once the vial exceeds ~0.12 g/L — but it applies to every LB line restarted from zero. Flagged for the operator, not corrected here.
pg_ramp.verified_with: tools/ramp_model.py, which imports the controller's own stepsize() and find_optimal_pump_volumes()

media_switch_policy.note: Switches are triggered by experimental milestones rather than a fixed interval. Each actual switch is logged as a 'media_switch' event carrying the trigger that fired.

design.imbalance_note: Design is damaged and only partly repaired. BL21-DE3 / LB / constant was empty after the vial 6 overheat and is now represented again by patrick-v07#2, but that vial's sleeve does not heat and the culture is growing at ~20 degC rather than 37, so it is not measured under the same conditions as any other line. BL21 / LB / constant remains a single unreplicated line. The BL21 / M9 replicate-2 vials on both units are merged lines carrying material spiked from their replicate-1 neighbours and are not independent replicates. plankton-v09 ended on 2026-08-24 with an efflux failure, leaving plankton's BL21 / M9 cell as one merged line only. Separately, the high-media lines for plankton vials 9 and 12 were exchanged in configuration from setup until 2026-08-25. Because vial 12 dilutes far more often than vial 9, the error is signed: plankton-v09 was over-dosed to the point of failure and plankton-v12 was under-dosed, so its apparent tolerance is inflated. Neither line's dose axis is usable. On 2026-08-26 patrick vials 4 and 6 were brought back with lineages branched from vials 5 and 7, so BL21/LB/constant and BL21-DE3/LB/constant each hold two lines again. Those pairs are clones that share their whole history up to the branch, not independent replicates: they answer what happens next from a common start, not whether the same outcome recurs independently. The same was done for patrick M9 at 16:30: vials 10 and 12 were emptied of their inviable contents and branched from vials 9 and 11. Every patrick cell now holds two lines, but all four pairs are clone pairs sharing their history up to today, so patrick currently supports questions about divergence from a common start and not about independent repetition.
design.switch_never_performed: As of 2026-08-26 no media switch has ever been performed. Every switch-mode line has run on a single media background for its whole life, media_switch_count is zero everywhere, and design.media_switch_policy.trigger_rule is still undefined. The constant/switch contrast is therefore nominal so far: the two arms differ in intent and in which unit they sit on, not yet in treatment.
design.replicate_structure_note: As of 2026-08-26 every one of the eight design cells holds two lines, and every pair was founded from a single donor on 26 Aug, with divergence times between 16:00 and 17:50 that hour. Three cells go further: BL21/M9/switch and BL21-DE3/LB/switch each hold two vessels seeded from the SAME 1 mL at the same moment, and both switch arms descend from constant-mode parents. Every one of these vessels is an independent evolutionary replicate from its own separation time, recorded per line in replicate_independence. The limit is not replication but resolution: with only hours of independent history, a variant shared by a pair cannot yet be told apart from standing variation carried in from the donor, so parallel evolution and shared ancestry are still confounded for anything predating 26 Aug. That resolves as independent history accumulates.

reservoirs.description: Each unit has its own independently prepared set of reservoirs: a low and a high PG reservoir for each media background. Reservoir ids are namespaced by unit ('<unit>/<media>-<pg g/L>') because patrick and plankton draw from separate bottles that are made, consumed and replaced independently. Since 2026-08-23T03:11-04:00 the LB low reservoir on both units carries 0.5 g/L PG rather than 0; the M9 low reservoirs remain at 0 g/L, so LB lines have a non-zero exposure floor and M9 lines do not.
reservoirs.volume_tracking: volume_prepared is what was made. current_volume is the best current estimate and level_source says how it was obtained: 'measured' when reported from an actual look at the bottle, 'prepared' when nothing has been measured since it was made — in which case current_volume is simply the prepared volume as of prepared_at, and any draw-down since then is inferred, not known. Consumption rates and depletion forecasts are derived from level_reading events by tools/media.py and are never stored as truth here. Readings may be qualified: 'at_least' values are lower bounds, so rates derived from them are upper bounds and the resulting time-to-empty is the earliest plausible, not the expected. A reservoir refilled or swapped keeps its id when the composition is unchanged; the outgoing bottle is preserved in fill_history and consumption accounting restarts at the new media_prep, since measuring across a refill would otherwise read as negative consumption.

inoculation_media.note: All 16 founder lines were inoculated into media containing 0 g/L PG on 22 Aug.

policy.rationale: Phloroglucinol degrades in solution, so a bottle's PG falls over its life. Small bottles replaced on a fixed schedule keep the delivered concentration close to nominal and avoid discarding large volumes when vials draw slowly. A side effect worth having: replacing on a schedule rather than on depletion removes the condition that caused both sipper-starvation incidents, since a bottle never gets low enough for the tube to draw air.
policy.note: M9 bottles at 500 mL. LB bottles at 1 L from 2026-08-27, high and low: both LB reservoirs ran dry inside twelve hours at the smaller sizes, and LB demand is the highest on the rig.

reservoirs.pg_stability_caveat: A reservoir's recorded PG is NOMINAL AT PREPARATION, not a constant. Phloroglucinol degrades in solution over a bottle's life, so the concentration actually delivered is at or below the figure recorded, and the gap widens with bottle age. No decay rate is assumed or modelled here — doing so would invent precision the log does not have. The consequence is that every delivered-dose estimate in this log is an UPPER BOUND, and the 2-3 day replacement cycle exists to keep that bound tight.

conventions.timestamps: ISO 8601 with explicit UTC offset, local time America/New_York. Approximate timestamps carry 'timestamp_precision'.
conventions.elapsed_time: elapsed_h is hours since the line's own t0 (its inoculation event), rounded to 2 decimals.
conventions.concentration: PG concentrations recorded as {value_g_per_L, value_mM} with g/L primary, converted using the anhydrous molar mass 126.11 g/mol.
conventions.quantities: Non-PG numeric parameters recorded as {value, unit} with SI-derived units (mL, uL, h, degC, per_h).
conventions.line_id: Base line_id is '<unit>-v<NN>' (e.g. 'patrick-v04'). Lineage identity is decoupled from hardware: a split creates child ids by appending '.a', '.b', ...; a merge joins its parents with '+'; and a vial that is emptied and re-seeded with a line that does NOT descend from its predecessor gets an occupancy suffix '#N' (e.g. 'patrick-v05#2' is the second culture to occupy patrick vial 5). Physical location lives in the 'unit' and 'vial' fields, which may change without changing the id.
conventions.event_id: 'EVT-<zero-padded 5-digit global counter>', monotonically increasing in order of logging (not necessarily in order of event timestamp).
conventions.event_ordering: Each line's 'events' array is maintained sorted by timestamp. Use event_id to recover logging order.
conventions.open_params: Every event carries a 'params' object with arbitrary key/value pairs. New experimental dimensions require no schema change; each new key is registered in 'parameter_registry'.
conventions.missing_data: Fields known to be missing are listed in the event's 'missing_fields' array rather than being silently omitted or guessed.
conventions.provenance: Events reconstructed from documents rather than logged live carry 'provenance': 'document' plus 'source_document'.
conventions.lineage: Lines form a directed acyclic graph. Each line's 'lineage.parents' lists immediate ancestors (empty for founders) and 'lineage.children' lists immediate descendants. A split terminates the parent and creates >=2 children; a merge creates one child with >=2 parents. 'lineage.roots' names the founder line(s) a node descends from and 'lineage.depth' is the number of split/merge steps from the founder. The events array of each line covers only that line's own interval, so a full history is read by walking parents. 'lineage.children' is derived from children's 'parents' and is rewritten on every update.
conventions.pg_exposure: Three different quantities, kept distinct. (1) The regime: the low and high reservoir concentrations a line is dosed between, which change only when media changes and are recorded here as events. (2) The vial concentration: controller state that moves on every dilution, owned by vialN_drugconc.txt and never transcribed by hand. (3) The delivered dose: the mean concentration of media actually pumped over an interval, derived by tools/media.py from the ratio of high to low reservoir volume drawn. At hold the high-media fraction sits close to vial_concentration / high_concentration, so reservoir levels give an independent read on where a line has got to even without the controller's files.
conventions.shared_events: A split is recorded once on the parent line it terminates; a merge is recorded once on the child line it creates. Each other line involved gets its own 'termination' event referencing that event_id. No event object is duplicated across lines, and any tooling that counts events must key on event_id anyway.
conventions.restarts_vs_descent: Re-seeding a vial from ancestor stock is not descent. Such a line is a founder with empty lineage.parents; the hardware relationship is recorded in lineage.occupies_vial_of and in the predecessor's replaced_by_line_ids. Only material continuity creates a lineage edge.
conventions.facility_events: Events that are not attributable to a single line (reservoir swaps, media prep, power loss) live in the top-level 'experiment_events' array. Each line they reach also carries its own event with 'caused_by_event' pointing at the facility event.
conventions.reservoir_id: '<unit>/<media>-<pg g/L>', e.g. 'plankton/LB-0.5'. Namespaced by unit because each eVOLVER has its own physically separate bottles. A change in PG concentration produces a new reservoir id and retires the old one, so a reservoir id always means one composition.
conventions.media_volumes: Media is made per setup rather than in batches, so each media_prep event both creates the media and fills the reservoir. Planning figures (consumption rate, days remaining) are derived from level_reading events by tools/media.py and are deliberately not stored in this file, so that only reported measurements are treated as fact.
conventions.merge_without_emptying: Spiking a culture into a vessel that still holds a standing population is a merge, not a re-seed: both populations contribute ancestry, so the resulting line carries both as parents. This is distinct from the flooding restarts, where the vessel was emptied and re-seeded from ancestor stock and the new line is a founder. The test is material continuity, not hardware.
conventions.controller_vs_physical: The controller's drug concentration is state it computes from intended pump volumes; it never observes the vessel. Normally the two agree closely enough to treat as one number. When a fault breaks that — a dry sipper, a failed pump, a manual override — the log records both: pg_controller_value as the setpoint that drives dosing, and pg_estimated_actual as an inferred physical state carrying its derivation and a confidence. Neither is allowed to stand in for the other.
conventions.ramp_history: Every line carries its own ramp history rather than inheriting a single global value, because target_ramp is a per-vial controller setting and lines begin, end and change at different times. Each entry gives the step size and the interval it applied over; an open 'to' means still in force. The first entry of every line is backfilled from the experiment design and has no set_by_event, since no discrete action set it — it was simply the value in force when the line began. design.pg_ramp remains the run-wide default; the per-line history is authoritative for any individual vial.
conventions.reservoir_positions_vs_bottles: A reservoir id names a hardware position on a unit, not a physical bottle. Bottles can be refilled in place or carried between units; either way the id stays and the bottle's identity is recorded in fill_history, with bottle_origin set when the contents arrived from another position. Media age is therefore read from bottle_origin.originally_prepared_at rather than from the position's prepared_at after a swap.
conventions.corrections: A reported value that turns out to be wrong is amended in place, but never silently: the event keeps corrected_from and corrected_at, its provenance becomes 'reported (corrected)', and the note says what changed and what conclusion, if any, was drawn from the wrong figure. The git history preserves the original entry independently.
conventions.error_provenance: An anomaly records what was observed; its root_cause records what is currently believed to explain it. When a later finding overturns the explanation, the observation stands and the diagnosis is retracted in place, with superseded_by_event pointing at the finding and the original text preserved. A log that quietly rewrites its own diagnoses cannot be used to reconstruct what was known when a decision was taken.
conventions.hardware_vs_line: A line's identity follows its culture, not the machine holding it. Vials can move between bodies and the lines continue unbroken, with no lineage edge, because nothing about the population changed. What does not follow the culture is everything belonging to the hardware: calibration, known faults and control addresses. A fault recorded against a vial position is recorded against the body it occurred on, so replacing the body clears it rather than carrying it forward.
conventions.branch_vs_split: Seeding a fresh vessel from a running culture is a BRANCH: the parent continues unbroken and the child carries one lineage edge. This differs from a split, where the parent ends and two or more children replace it, and from a merge, where a culture is added to a vessel that already holds a population and both contribute ancestry. The test is what happened to the parent and whether the destination was empty. A branch's child is an independent evolutionary replicate of its parent from the moment of separation and shares everything before it; the line records that moment in replicate_independence. See the replicates convention.
conventions.controller_run_restarts: The controller's experiment directory can be restarted without touching the cultures. When that happens the lines continue unbroken — identity follows the culture — but the controller clock returns to zero and its pump and concentration logs start empty. Anything derived from those files is therefore split across runs and must be carried forward deliberately: generations_carried_forward on each line holds what accrued under previous runs, and the live feed only ever counts the current one.
conventions.schema_versioning: schema_version is the shape of this file, not the state of the experiment. It changes only when a structural change would break a reader: a new required field, a renamed block, a changed value type. New event types, new params keys and new conventions do NOT bump it, because absorbing those without a schema change is the point of the open params block and the parameter registry. 1.2.0 records the structures added since 1.1.0 -- per-line ramp history, reservoir fill history and policy, controller block, generations carried forward, and the correction fields -- none of which invalidate a 1.1.0 reader.
conventions.replicates: Vessels separated from a common donor are independent replicates from the moment of separation -- a child branched off a continuing parent, and two vessels seeded from the same 1 mL at the same instant, equally. Clone is not a useful category in an evolution experiment: the populations diverge by definition, and the question the design asks is what they diverge into. What must be recorded instead is the DIVERGENCE TIME, because it bounds what the replication covers: everything after it is independent across vessels, everything before it is shared, so a variant seen in two siblings may be one pre-branch event rather than parallel evolution. Merge children are the exception -- they physically contain material from another line, so their ancestry is mixed rather than merely shared, and patrick-v09+v10 and plankton-v09+v10 keep the stronger caveat. Set by EVT-00258, superseding the earlier clone framing.
conventions.pg_high_max_reached: Line-level field: the highest HIGH-RESERVOIR concentration the line has been configured against, not the highest concentration the culture actually reached. Adopted 2026-08-27 on the operator's statement that every high reservoir in the current setup is 5 g/L (EVT-00282). Every line in the log reads 5 g/L, so no existing value distinguishes this from the alternative reading; a line configured against a different high reservoir would separate them, and the intended meaning should be restated at that point rather than inferred from these entries. For actual exposure use pg_regime.vial_concentration and the delivered dose from tools/media.py, which are different quantities again -- see the pg_exposure convention.
conventions.ramp_step_history: The ramp step is uniform across the rig at any given moment but has changed once: 0.05 g/L from t0, doubled to 0.1 g/L on 2026-08-24T09:00 by EVT-00088. A statement that 'the ramp is 0.1' describes the current configuration and must not be backfilled onto ramp.history, where 20 lines carry a 0.05 segment. On an ended line ramp.current is null by design -- the line has no current ramp -- and that null is not a missing value. Confirmed for the current setup by EVT-00282.

event_types.inoculation: Initial seeding of a vessel from an outgrowth culture; defines the line's t0.
event_types.pg_change: Any change in phloroglucinol exposure, whether an automated deterministic ramp step or a manual override.
event_types.media_switch: Change of media background (LB <-> M9) for a switch-mode line.
event_types.reading: OD, growth-rate, or other quantitative measurement.
event_types.sampling: Removal of material for glycerol stocks, plating, DNA extraction, or sequencing.
event_types.phenotyping: Characterization of a line's phenotype (MIC, IC50, growth curve, plate assay). Often the decision point that motivates a subsequent split or merge.
event_types.split: A line is divided into two or more descendant lines, typically following phenotyping. Terminates the parent and creates the children.
event_types.merge: Two or more lines are combined into a single descendant line. Terminates the parents and creates one child with multiple entries in lineage.parents.
event_types.anomaly: Unplanned deviation: contamination, hardware failure, evaporation, power loss.
event_types.intervention: Deliberate corrective action taken in response to an anomaly or a decision point.
event_types.controller_config_change: Change to eVOLVER control parameters, ramp logic, or firmware.
event_types.note: Free observation with no structured action attached.
event_types.termination: End of a line, with reason.
event_types.reservoir_change: Facility-level change to a shared media reservoir. Recorded once in experiment_events, with a per-line pg_change event for each line it reaches.
event_types.media_prep: Preparation of a volume of media and its loading into a named reservoir. Media is made per setup, so a prep and a reservoir fill are the same action.
event_types.level_reading: Reported remaining volume in a reservoir at a point in time. The only measured input to consumption estimates.
event_types.reservoir_retired: A reservoir taken off line, whether exhausted or replaced.
event_types.reservoir_swap: Two reservoir bottles exchanged between units, or one moved to a different position, with no change of composition. Reservoir ids name hardware positions and do not move; the contents, age and provenance do, so consumption accounting restarts on both sides.
event_types.hardware_swap: Vials moved to different physical hardware with their cultures intact. The lines continue unbroken — identity follows the culture, not the machine — but calibration, faults and control addresses belong to the hardware and do not move with them.

inoculum_volume.description: Volume of saturated outgrowth culture transferred into the vial.

culture_volume.description: Working volume of the culture vessel.

dilution_factor.description: Fold dilution of the inoculum into the target media.

source_culture.description: Description of the material used to inoculate. Descriptive provenance, not biological ancestry: naming a prior line's id in this free text (e.g. '1 mL of patrick-v05#2') is prose a reader can follow, exactly like notes -- it never creates lineage.parents or any other structured link back to that line. This is the correct way to record that a new culture's material came from a specific prior lineage, including an already-ENDED one -- branch/split/merge can never express that, since all three require an ACTIVE parent (409 otherwise), and restart's own predecessor_line_id records hardware/vial continuity only, never descent.

ic50.description: Half-maximal inhibitory PG concentration for the line.
ic50.note: Registered in advance; not yet used by any logged event.

termination_reason.description: Why a line ended (split, merge, contamination, planned end).

incident_id.description: Identifier grouping every event that belongs to one incident.

vials_affected.description: Physical vials involved in an incident, as written on the hardware.

replaced_by_line_ids.description: Line(s) that take over this line's vial position without inheriting its evolutionary history. Deliberately distinct from lineage.children, which implies descent.

predecessor_in_vial.description: Line that previously occupied this vial. Records hardware continuity only, not descent.

reservoir_id_from.description: Reservoir in use before a media or reservoir change.

reservoir_id_to.description: Reservoir in use after a media or reservoir change.

lines_affected.description: Lines a facility-level event applies to.

volume_prepared.description: Volume of media made and loaded into the reservoir.

volume_remaining.description: Reported remaining volume at the time of a level reading.

level_source.description: 'measured' if reported from the bottle, 'prepared' if never checked since making it.

role.description: Whether the reservoir is the low or high PG feed.

unit.description: eVOLVER unit a facility-level event applies to.

replaces.description: Reservoir this one takes over from.

replaced_by.description: Reservoir taking over from this one.

measurement_qualifier.description: How precise a reported volume is: 'exact' when read off a graduation, 'approximate' for an eyeballed value, 'at_least' when reported as a lower bound (e.g. '>750 mL'). A lower bound means consumption is an upper bound, so any time-to-empty derived from it is the earliest it could happen, not the expected.

observation_type.description: Kind of qualitative observation recorded in a note event (e.g. growth_rate_trend, turbidity, colour, foaming). Qualitative by definition — values, when they exist, belong in a reading.

caused_by_anomaly.description: Event id of the anomaly that forced this action.

purpose.description: Why material was removed from a line.

destination_line_ids.description: Lines that material removed by a sampling event went into.

previous_fill_remaining.description: Volume still in the outgoing bottle when a reservoir was swapped rather than run dry.

duration.description: How long a fault or condition persisted.

previous_ramp_step_size.description: target_ramp before a controller config change.

controller_parameter.description: Name of the controller setting that changed.

pg_controller_value.description: The concentration the controller holds as state and doses from. Authoritative for what the pumps will do, not for what is in the vessel.

pg_controller_value_before.description: Controller concentration immediately before a manual override.

pg_estimated_actual.description: Inferred physical concentration in the vessel when it is known to differ from the controller's value. Model-derived, never a measurement.

pg_estimate_basis.description: How an estimated physical concentration was derived, including assumptions.

pg_estimate_confidence.description: low, medium or high confidence in an inferred value.

volume_to_plankton.description: Volume the plankton position holds after a swap.

volume_to_patrick.description: Volume the patrick position holds after a swap.

state_before.description: Level, prepared volume and prep time of each position immediately before a swap.

corrected_from.description: The value originally reported for a field that was later corrected. Kept so the record shows what was believed at the time and what replaced it, rather than quietly presenting the correction as if it had always been there.

corrected_at.description: When a previously reported value was corrected.

od_reliable.description: False when a vial's optical readings cannot be trusted, e.g. because the vessel over-filled and the optical path changed.

starting_od.description: Optical density at which a restarted line was handed to the controller.

transcription_resolved.description: True when a dictated reading was ambiguous and the reservoir it belongs to was inferred rather than stated. The reasoning is in the event note; the operator should confirm.

pg_exposure_error.description: Direction of a known error in a line's PG exposure: received_none, received_double, received_partial, received_excess, received_deficit, or exchanged_with_partner when a swap's direction cannot be resolved. An exchange between vials with different dilution rates resolves to excess on the slower vial and deficit on the faster one, since each is dosed on its partner's schedule.

pg_reliable.description: False when a line's recorded PG concentrations cannot be trusted, independently of whether its OD can.

superseded_by_event.description: Event whose finding overturned this event's diagnosis.

error_class.description: Whether a fault was hardware, configuration, media or procedure.

discovered_at.description: When a fault was found, as distinct from when it began.

effective_from.description: When a configuration took effect, which for an error discovered later is when it began rather than when it was found. Paired with discovered_at.

fault_mode.description: How a fault acted: 'exchanged' when two channels were swapped with each other, as distinct from one being redirected or lost. The distinction matters because an exchange leaves both parties dosed, just wrongly.

partner_vial.description: The vial this one was exchanged with.

direction_basis.description: How the sign of an exposure error was determined.

batch_id.description: Groups samples taken together in one round.

method.description: How a sample was taken or handled, e.g. spot plate, streak, glycerol stock.

plate_media.description: Media of the plate a sample was spotted on.

plate_pg.description: PG concentration of the plate. Zero means the sample was plated non-selectively.

volume_primed.description: Volume drawn from a reservoir to fill tubing rather than to feed a vial. Not chargeable to culture consumption.

superseded_reason.description: Why an earlier assessment was withdrawn. Paired with an event whose type was downgraded from anomaly to note, so the withdrawal is visible without leaving a false anomaly flag in place.

affected_scope.description: How far an anomaly reaches: this vial only, all vials on a reservoir, a whole unit. Named distinctly from the top-level 'scope' field, which says whether an event is line- or facility-level.

spot_result.description: Appearance of a spot plate: confluent_lawn, discrete_colonies, or no_growth.

viable_cfu_per_mL.description: Viable count inferred from a spot plate. Read with cfu_direction.

cfu_direction.description: Whether viable_cfu_per_mL is 'about', 'at_least' (a lawn, too numerous to count) or 'at_most' (no growth, below detection).

colony_count.description: Colonies counted on a spot. Null when confluent.

sampled_at.description: When the sample was taken, as distinct from when it was read.

what_moved.description: What physically changed hands in a hardware swap.

downtime.description: How long the affected vials were not under control.

pumps_moved.description: Whether pumps moved with the body, which decides if pump calibration survives.

pump_calibration_valid.description: Whether pump_cal.json still describes the hardware in use.

od_calibration_reloaded.description: Whether per-sleeve OD calibration was redone for new hardware.

control_ip_changed.description: Whether the unit's control address changed.

previous_fill_remaining_basis.description: Where the outgoing volume figure came from: measured at the swap, or carried from the last reading. The distinction matters when a bottle sat for hours between the two.

controller_initial_concentration.description: The concentration the controller was told a vial starts at. Distinct from the media's concentration: they agree only if set deliberately.

input_pump2.description: Controller setting naming the pump that delivers HIGH-PG media to a vial. Recorded explicitly at founding because a mis-set input_pump2 caused INC-0004, where two vials' high lines were exchanged for the whole run without anything failing visibly.

cultures_disturbed.description: Whether a controller-side change touched the cultures. False means bookkeeping only, and no lineage or biological consequence follows.

old_exp_name.description: Controller experiment directory in use before a restart. Needed to find the pump log that generations must be carried forward from.

new_exp_name.description: Controller experiment directory in use after a restart.

units.description: eVOLVER units a facility-level change applies to.

reservoir_empty.description: Anomaly type: a reservoir ran dry, so commanded doses from it delivered nothing. Distinct from sipper_above_media_line, where liquid remained but the tube could not reach it.

supersedes.description: Event whose finding or framing this event replaces. The superseded event is never edited; this is the forward pointer that makes the replacement visible from the new event.

affected_line_ids.description: Lines whose records a facility-scope event changes, where the event is not itself a lineage operation on them.

confirms_events.description: Events whose values the operator has since confirmed. The confirmed events are not edited: this is the forward pointer that closes a gap without rewriting what was known at the time. Distinct from supersedes, which replaces a finding rather than confirming it.

resolves_missing_fields.description: Entries in the named events' missing_fields that this event answers. Those arrays stay as written -- they were accurate when written -- so anything reporting open gaps must subtract what later events resolve.

applies_to.description: Scope of a confirmation or statement: 'current configuration' when it describes the rig as it now stands and must NOT be backfilled onto history. Added because the operator's ramp confirmation was true of the current setup but not of the run, which had a 0.05 g/L step until 2026-08-24.

new_unit.description: The hardware unit a line's culture was physically relocated to by a line-scoped hardware_swap -- distinct from the facility-level hardware.units.*.body_change fields, which track a whole unit's own chassis history, not a single line's position.

new_vial.description: The vial number a line's culture was physically relocated to by a line-scoped hardware_swap.

previous_unit.description: The hardware unit a line's culture occupied immediately before a line-scoped hardware_swap relocated it -- optional, but when supplied must match the line's actual current unit at write time (ISSUE_002), the same precedent media_switch's media_from already sets.

previous_vial.description: The vial number a line's culture occupied immediately before a line-scoped hardware_swap relocated it -- optional, but when supplied must match the line's actual current vial at write time (ISSUE_002).

vacate.description: ISSUE_002 follow-up: marks a line-scoped hardware_swap as removing the culture from the evolver entirely, rather than relocating it -- line.unit/vial both become null, a real 'not currently on any evolver' state, not a missing value. Mutually exclusive with new_unit/new_vial in the same event: a reciprocal swap between two lines (each destination momentarily occupied by the other) is logged as two ordinary events per line -- vacate first, then a second hardware_swap with new_unit/new_vial to the real destination -- never as one event doing both, and never as a multi-line atomic write.

reactivate.description: Marks a media_prep against an EXISTING, currently-retired reservoir as deliberately bringing it back into active service -- reservoirItem.status flips retired -> active as part of the same write, alongside the ordinary volume_prepared/pg/current_volume fields a media_prep always moves. Explicit, not inferred: a media_prep naming a retired reservoir_id without reactivate:true still records the fresh volume/pg (the physical fact of what was prepared is never withheld), but leaves status untouched and says so in the response -- a retired reservoir's status is a deliberate administrative fact (contamination, decommissioned, etc.), and flipping it back as an unannounced side effect of any media_prep that happens to name that id would risk exactly the silent, unintended reactivation this flag exists to prevent. Reactivating an already-active reservoir is a harmless no-op, not an error, mirroring hardware_swap's own vacate precedent for confirming state that already holds.

events.notes:
The high-media sipper on patrick/M9-5 reached the falling liquid level and this vial's tube was found partly air-filled, so its last dispense — probably its last few — delivered less high media than commanded, or none. It was therefore UNDER-dosed across the window and its recorded PG overstates what it received.

Scope is this vial alone. An earlier version of this entry extended it to all four lines fed by patrick/M9-5, reasoning from a ~90%% shortfall in the bottle's draw. The operator's observation settles it the other way: the other three tubes were still full of media, and a tube only draws air if its pump runs while the sipper is dry. The bottle shortfall is instead evidence that this vial accounts for most of patrick M9-5's normal draw — which follows, since the other three dilute infrequently.

Onset is estimated at 19:25 on 25 Aug, when the bottle reached ~100 mL, and is inferred rather than observed.

Confluent growth across the spot, the expected result for a healthy culture. Too numerous to count, so viability is a lower bound only: a confluent 10 uL spot needs on the order of 10^4-10^5 CFU/mL. This assay separates viable from inviable; it does not rank the healthy ones against each other.

params.method: vial moved to the same position on a new eVOLVER body

events.notes: Paused for about 18 minutes while the body was changed. No dilutions in that window, so nothing is excluded from this line's generation count — there is simply nothing there to count. The culture sat at ambient without stirring or temperature control for the duration, which is short enough to be unremarkable for E. coli but is recorded because it is a real interruption in an otherwise continuous selection.

Low reservoir raised from 0 to 1 g/L PG. This line's exposure floor is now 1 g/L: if it currently sits below that it will be carried up within a few dilutions, and the growth gate cannot hold it back.

events.notes: The high pump ran but delivered air for roughly 8 h, so the only liquid entering this vial was low media at 0.5 g/L. Two consequences. The drug washed out of the vessel: at the controller's own commanded volumes (4.09 mL low per cycle into 22 mL) and the measured draw of 11.5 mL/h per line, the half-life is about 1 h, so a vial at 3.2 g/L would have fallen to ~2.1 g/L after 1 h, ~0.9 after 4 h and ~0.56 by the 8 h mark — effectively the low reservoir. And the controller's recorded concentration kept rising throughout, because it computes concentration from intended pump volumes and never from what actually arrives. Start time is estimated, not observed.

params.pg_estimate_basis: Washout model run on the controller's own find_optimal_pump_volumes at the concentration it believed (3.2 g/L), giving 4.09 mL of low media per cycle into a 22 mL vial, combined with the measured low draw of 11.5 mL/h per line over the interval. 2.81 cycles/h, 22 cycles across the 8 h fault, decaying toward the 0.5 g/L low reservoir with a half-life near 1 h.

events.notes: Controller drug concentration manually set to 3.2 g/L on all four plankton LB vials. It had drifted HIGHER than this during the 8 h sipper fault, because it accumulates concentration from intended pump volumes and never observes what arrives; 3.2 g/L is the last value the operator trusts, roughly where the vials stood when the high feed went dry. The physical concentration is a separate quantity and is estimated at ~0.56 g/L, since the drug washed out while the controller's figure climbed. The two are recorded side by side deliberately: 3.2 is the setpoint of record that will drive dosing from here, 0.56 is an inferred physical state with the assumptions above and is not a measurement. Dosing from a believed 3.2 will pull the real concentration back up to roughly that value within about 3 h, which is far faster than the ramp that originally took it there.

events.notes: eVOLVER pumpcontrol_ramp 'setpoint' for plankton vial 3 (line plankton-v03) changed from 50000 to 49000 via POST /config, at operator request. This is the OD-based dilution-trigger threshold in experiment_parameters.yaml, not a PG/media quantity, and has no registered params key for its value. The before/after (50000 -> 49000) is recorded in 'reason' only as a workaround to satisfy this server's requirement that a controller_config_change name more than just controller_parameter -- 'reason' is not semantically the right field (it registers 'why', not 'what changed') and this event's actual meaning is fully captured here in notes instead. Server response confirmed the write (written: true) and reported this field under live_reload.applies_without_restart, i.e. no eVOLVER process restart is needed for it to take effect. A real params key for this setting's value should be registered so future events like this don't need this workaround.

Being drawn from one donor at one moment makes the two vessels identical at that instant and nothing after it: mutation, drift and selection act independently in each from then on, so they are replicates of everything that happens downstream, as is the continuing parent. What the replication does not cover is anything already present in the donor at 2026-08-26T17:50. A variant found in two of these vessels may be a single pre-branch event carried into each rather than parallel evolution, so date any shared variant against the divergence time before reading it as convergent. A branch: only the donor contributes ancestry, and the donor continues running in its own vial. This is one of three vials replaced from the same donor at this time, the other two being the remaining entries of that round. The final culture volume after dilution was not reported, so the donor's dilution factor cannot be computed and the vial's starting PG is unknown: the donor carried a live controller concentration that was neither read nor supplied, and 2 mL of it entered an unrecorded volume of 0 g/L M9. Mode and replicate are carried forward from the vial's previous occupant, not from the donor: the donor patrick-v09#3 runs in 'constant' mode, and mode cannot be changed after a line is created, so the vial's existing controller slot was preserved rather than the donor's. The operator did not report a design change, but neither value was explicitly confirmed and both are named in missing_fields. Strain comes from the donor (BL21), which matches the outgoing occupant in every case, so no strain conflict arises. Time is the operator's approximate report of about 11 AM on 2026-08-30, not an observed clock reading; this round was logged on 2026-08-31, the day after it happened.

Time is the operator's approximate report of about 11 AM, not an observed clock reading; timestamp_precision is 'hour'. About 10 uL was drawn from this vial and spotted onto LB agar, as part of a round covering all 16 active vials on both units. The volume is the operator's approximation ('about 10 uL'), not a measured delivery. The plate was described only as LB agar with no additive named, so it is recorded as plain non-selective LB at 0 g/L PG following the convention of the 2026-08-29 round (EVT-00394 onward); that reading is not separately confirmed and is flagged. It was also not reported whether all 16 spots share one plate or each vial got its own, so no plate identifier is recorded. Being non-selective, this records viability and yields pickable colonies; it does not preserve or measure the population's tolerance distribution, and any colony taken from it has passed through a step with no phloroglucinol. No plate result was available at the time of plating.

target_ramp doubled from 0.05 to 0.1 g/L per successful ramp, on every line, to reach working concentrations sooner and cut total media use. Verified against the controller's own functions: this does not change media use per hour, since every dilution cycle dispenses a fixed 10 mL whatever the ramp is. plankton's experiment_parameters.yaml had input_pump2 swapped between vials 9 and 12, in force from setup on 22 Aug until discovery. input_pump2 names the pump that delivers HIGH-PG media, so the two high lines were exchanged: when vial 12 called for a dose it went into vial 9, and when vial 9 called for one it went into vial 12.

Each vial therefore DID receive high-PG media, and each was under real selection. What each received was the other's dose — the other vial's timing, the other vial's computed volume, driven by the other vial's OD and ramp state. Both vials' recorded concentrations are wrong, and the direction is NOT known: it depends on how the two vials' ramp positions and dilution frequencies compared at each moment. A vial whose partner was further up the ramp was over-dosed relative to its record; one whose partner lagged was under-dosed. Low media was unaffected throughout, since each vial's low pump was correctly assigned.

The volume imbalance is what made it visible. A vial's efflux runs only after its OWN dispense events, so the high-media volume arriving from the partner's dispense was never removed. Both vials accumulated volume; vial 9 was the one seen overflowing, and vial 12 should be checked for the same, since the mechanism applies equally to it and an over-filled vessel also corrupts its OD readings.

CORRECTED 2026-08-25T16:20:00-04:00: the first version of this entry described the fault as vial 9 receiving no high media and vial 12 receiving its own plus vial 9's. That was wrong. The two high-PG lines were EXCHANGED, so each vial received high media on the other vial's schedule and in the other vial's computed volume, and neither received its own. The original text is superseded, not deleted.

MECHANISM, from the operator's reading of the dilution data 2026-08-25T16:35. The exchange is not symmetric in effect, because the two vials dilute at very different rates. Vial 12 (BL21-DE3) has been diluting frequently while vial 9 (BL21) stopped growing some time ago. Under the exchange, every one of vial 12's frequent triggers sent a high-PG dose into vial 9, while vial 9's rare triggers sent almost nothing into vial 12.

The error is therefore signed, not indeterminate as an earlier version of this entry concluded:
  vial 9  was OVER-dosed. Its true exposure exceeds its record, by a lot.
  vial 12 was UNDER-dosed. Its true exposure falls short of its record.

Vial 9 is a positive feedback loop, which is what makes this more than a bookkeeping error. Slower growth meant fewer of its own triggers, but its partner's triggers carried on regardless, so more PG arrived while the culture was less able to handle it. None of those doses were followed by an efflux cycle, since efflux runs only after a vial's own dispenses, so both PG and volume accumulated. That accounts for the sickness, the failure to grow, and the over-filling in one mechanism rather than three.

Directly testable against the pump logs, which already hold everything needed: vial 12's in2 volumes are the PG that actually entered vial 9, and vial 9's in2 volumes are what actually entered vial 12. Their dispense counts should differ sharply.

experiment_events.notes:
Sleeves were tested on the new body before the move, vials went back to their own numbered positions, and the unit keeps the name 'patrick'. Three things follow, and they pull in different directions.

Pumps did not move, so pump_cal.json still describes the hardware in use. Every volume, burn rate and generation count derived from pump timing carries through this swap unbroken. That is the reason the media and generation records need no window excluded here.

OD is a different matter, and the operator's practice is what saves it: raw sensor values are used rather than converted OD, so a stale per-sleeve calibration does not propagate into the control loop. Where a new sleeve's dynamic range differed, the per-vial threshold was adjusted to match. Those adjustments are real controller changes and are recorded separately; the vials and values were not captured.

The control IP changed. evolver_api resolves the unit name from experiment_settings.ip through dashboard's IP table, so an unrecognised address makes /api/v1/health report no evolver name. It degrades rather than breaks — the viewer only rejects a unit that answers for a DIFFERENT name, not one that answers for none — but identity confirmation is lost until the new address is added to the table, or better, until evolver_name is set explicitly in experiment_parameters.yaml. The name is the thing being kept stable here, so it should not be inferred from an address that just changed.

Per-vial dilution thresholds adjusted on those patrick vials whose new sleeve had a different sensor dynamic range. Which vials, and the old and new values, were not recorded. This matters for reading the data either side of the swap: the threshold sets the density a culture is held at, so dilution FREQUENCY before and after is not comparable on any vial that was adjusted. Generation counts are unaffected, since each dispense dilutes by the same volume ratio regardless of the threshold that triggered it.

M9 low raised from PG-free to 1 g/L on both units; M9 high unchanged at 5 g/L. The M9 exposure envelope is now 1-5 g/L rather than 0-5.

This has an effect the growth gate cannot override. Pure low media now carries 1 g/L, so any M9 vial below that is pushed upward whatever its growth is doing: from 0 g/L the smallest achievable move is about +0.34 g/L per cycle, and roughly +0.41 in the bootstrap branch. An M9 vial under 1 g/L converges on 1 g/L within three or four dilutions regardless of whether the controller wants to hold it.

It also cuts high-media demand in the short term. Below about 1 g/L the optimiser draws NO high media at all, since low media alone already exceeds the target, so the M9-5 bottles will be drawn on less until their vials climb past the new floor.

params.reason: start clean experiment directories so the eVOLVER monitor reads clearly

experiment_events.notes:
Fresh experiment runs started on both units. The cultures were not touched; this is a bookkeeping restart on the controller side.

It does reset the controller clock and start empty pump_log and drugconc files, which has three consequences worth having written down.

The viewer would have gone permanently blind without a fix. It tracks a per-vial high-water mark and asks for events after it; with the clock back at zero that mark sits in the future forever, so no new dispense would ever be fetched. It also re-anchors cached events using the current elapsed time, which would have dragged every event from the old run forward into the future and corrupted the generation counts. Both are now caught by detecting a changed run name or a clock that has gone backwards, and clearing that vial's cache.

Burn rates will read low for the first few hours: the trailing window still spans time before the restart, when the new log had no events. It corrects itself once the window has passed.

Generations accumulated before the restart are NOT in the new pump log and cannot be recovered from the live API. They remain on disk in the old experiment directories. tools/carry_generations.py reads a finished directory and records the totals per line as generations_carried_forward, which the viewer adds to what it counts live. Until that is run, every line's generation count restarts from zero and understates its history.

media.py is unaffected: it reads reservoir levels from this log and never touched the controller's files.

params.superseded_reason: EVT-00221 described plankton-v12#2 as a clone of plankton-v11 rather than an independent replicate. The operator has ruled that framing wrong in principle, so it is withdrawn here rather than left standing as the log's position.

experiment_events.notes:
Operator ruling on how sibling and branch lineages are counted, applied across the log.

The log had been recording every vessel seeded from a running culture as NOT an independent replicate -- and, where two vessels were filled from the same 1 mL at the same instant, as two vessels holding one lineage. The operator's correction: they will drift apart by definition, so clone loses its meaning in an evolution experiment. They are to be treated as replicates.

This is right, and the old wording confused two different things. Being founded from one donor makes two vessels identical at the instant of separation and at no time after it. Mutation, drift and selection then act independently in each, which is exactly what replication in an evolution experiment means: the replicated object is the evolutionary process, not the starting genotype. Sharing a starting point is the design, not a defect in it.

What survives from the old note, in narrower form: the replication is bounded by the divergence time. Anything already segregating in the donor is shared, so a variant found in both members of a pair may be one pre-branch event rather than two independent ones. That is a constraint on reading convergence, not on calling them replicates, and it weakens as independent history accumulates. Every affected line therefore now carries its divergence time as the operative field, and the previous wording is preserved alongside it in replicate_independence_superseded.

Scope: the nine branch-derived lines listed in affected_line_ids, the branch_vs_split convention, and the design-level note (renamed from clone_pairs_note to replicate_structure_note). A new replicates convention states the rule for future entries.

Deliberately NOT changed: patrick-v09+v10 and plankton-v09+v10. Those are merge children that physically carry material spiked from the very line they would be compared against, so their ancestry is mixed rather than shared from a clean point, and no divergence time describes them. Both ended on 26 Aug. The caveat in design.imbalance_note stands for them.

Unrelated staleness noticed while editing and left alone: design.imbalance_note still says plankton's BL21 / M9 cell is one merged line only, which predates plankton-v12#2, v13 and v14.

Seven M9 lines failed to grow and were terminated together at 16:50. Two were established cultures running since 22 Aug (patrick-v09, patrick-v11); five were seeded from them on 26 Aug and never established.

The common factor is the medium, not the lineage. Every failed line draws M9, on both eVOLVER bodies, across both strains and both modes. Every LB line on both units is still running: plankton-v03, plankton-v04, patrick-v05#2, patrick-v07#2, patrick-v04#2, patrick-v06#3, plankton-v05#2, plankton-v06#2. A failure that crosses units, strains and modes but stops at the medium boundary points at the M9 itself or at what was done to it, not at the hardware and not at the cultures.

One event fits that boundary. Per EVT-00201 the M9 low reservoirs went from 0 to 1 g/L PG on 26 Aug at 15:40. Until then these lines had never seen phloroglucinol at all: their floor was zero, so the step was from naive straight to a 1 g/L floor, and a raised low reservoir is not subject to the growth gate -- pure low media carries the drug, so every vial is carried up within a few dilutions whatever its growth is doing. An hour later five of them were re-seeded into fresh 1 g/L M9, which is a 1 g/L challenge to an inoculum with no acclimation at all. The LB lines are also at a 1 g/L floor and are fine, but they ramped to it from 0.5 and they are in rich medium, where tolerance to a phenolic is expected to be higher than in minimal.

This is a hypothesis that fits the boundary, NOT a diagnosis. It has not been tested, and at least two alternatives fit as well: a bad M9 batch (both units' M9 was prepared from the same stock), and the 11:00 PG reset on 27 Aug whose values were never recorded. root_cause stays null until something distinguishes them.

Cheapest available test, and it expires: read the levels on all four M9 bottles now. All four were prepared at 11:00 today, so a reading taken at termination measures a clean ~6 h window. Cultures that were not growing were not diluting, so near-untouched bottles would confirm the failure physically and date its onset against the LB bottles over the same hours. Once the vials are cleared or re-seeded that window is gone.

OD and PG history are both marked reliable: nothing here says the instruments were wrong, only that the cultures did not grow. A vial that is not diluting is not accumulating generations either, so the generation counts for these lines are flat over the window rather than wrong.

The M9 arm rebuilt 28 minutes after it was terminated. Seven LB lines each gave 1 mL into a cleared vial of fresh 1 g/L M9; all seven donors continue in LB. Every transfer stayed inside its own unit, so mode follows both the parent and the existing mode/unit confound: patrick constant, plankton switch.

The design is whole again on paper. Sixteen active lines, all eight cells at two replicates, for the first time since the 23 Aug flooding. Two qualifications on reading it that way.

FIRST, the cells are not equally replicated, and the vial ages hide it. What bounds a within-cell comparison is when the two lines' ancestors separated, not when the vials were seeded:
  BL21/M9/constant -- patrick-v09#2 and patrick-v10#4 descend from patrick-v04#2 and patrick-v05#2, which separated on 26 Aug 16:00. About 25 h of independent history.
  BL21-DE3/M9/constant -- patrick-v11#2 and patrick-v12#3 descend from patrick-v06#3 and patrick-v07#2, separated on 26 Aug 16:00. Same 25 h.
  BL21/M9/switch -- plankton-v13#2 and plankton-v14#2 descend from plankton-v03 and plankton-v04, separate founders since t0. Five days, and the best-replicated cell in the experiment.
  BL21-DE3/M9/switch -- plankton-v11 and plankton-v12#3 are not replicates of each other in any useful sense. plankton-v11 has been in M9 continuously since t0 and has never seen LB; plankton-v12#3 arrives from four days in LB. They share a cell label and nothing else. Any comparison inside this cell is confounded with media history.

SECOND, this is an unplanned test of INC-0009, and the prediction is recorded now so it cannot be reconstructed favourably later. Twenty-eight minutes ago seven M9 lines failed under what looked like a naive step to a 1 g/L floor in minimal medium. These seven meet the same floor, but their inocula are already held at 1 g/L in LB. If they grow, the earlier failure was about the absence of prior PG exposure rather than about the M9 itself, and INC-0009's leading hypothesis stands. If they fail the same way, that hypothesis is in trouble and suspicion moves to the M9 preparation shared by both units, or to the medium-drug interaction being lethal regardless of adaptation. Either outcome is informative, which is the one good thing about the timing.

The confound to keep in view either way: a spike from LB into M9 changes the carbon source and the drug background at the same time, so a failure does not decompose into which of the two caused it without a control this design does not currently carry -- an LB-adapted line moved into M9 at 0 g/L would be that control, and no vial is running it.

Reading the four M9 bottle levels still matters and still expires: they were prepared at 11:00 and the terminated cultures have now been replaced, so the last clean window on whether those vials were drawing media at all closed at 17:18.

Operator confirms THE CURRENT SETUP: every ramp step size is 0.1 g/L and every high reservoir is 5 g/L. This is a statement about the configuration as it now stands, not about the whole run, and the distinction is the reason this note exists rather than a bare edit.

The ramp has not always been 0.1. Per EVT-00088 the step was doubled from 0.05 to 0.1 g/L on 24 Aug at 09:00, on every line then running; 20 lines carry a 0.05 segment in ramp.history and those segments stay exactly as they are. Two of the earliest anomalies -- patrick-v10 and plankton-v10, both 'presumed failure to survive the initial ramp' -- happened while the step was 0.05, so flattening the history to a uniform 0.1 would quietly falsify the conditions under which they failed. 30 of 37 lines carry a current ramp and all read 0.1; the other seven read null because they ended before 24 Aug and have no current ramp at all. That null is correct and is not a gap to be filled.

High reservoirs are 5 g/L on all 37 lines with no exceptions anywhere in the log, past or present.

This closes ramp_step_size_confirmed on the seven inoculation events in confirms_events. Those events keep their missing_fields as written -- the flag was accurate when written, since the value had been carried over from each vial's previous occupant rather than re-read. Anything counting open gaps must subtract resolves_missing_fields rather than reading missing_fields alone.

input_pump2 is NOT covered and stays open on all seven. A mis-set input_pump2 produced INC-0004, so it is worth reading off the controller rather than assuming it followed the vial.

This also settles what pg_high_max_reached means, a field carrying no registry or convention entry and reading two ways: the highest high reservoir a line has been configured against, or the highest concentration it actually reached. Both give 5 g/L for every line, because no line has ever been configured against a different high reservoir, so no existing value distinguishes them. Adopting the configured-ceiling reading on the operator's statement. If a line is ever given a different high reservoir the two part company immediately, and which is meant should be restated then rather than inferred from these entries.

experiment_events.notes:
Correction to the M9 bottle claim in EVT-00259. That event said the four M9 bottles were prepared at 11:00 on 27 Aug, and that reading them at termination would give a clean ~6 h window isolating whether the failing vials were drawing media at all.

Both halves are wrong. All four M9 bottles were prepared on 26 Aug at 15:40 (EVT-00196, EVT-00197, EVT-00198, EVT-00199). The 11:00 preparations on 27 Aug were the two LB LOW bottles (EVT-00243, EVT-00245) and nothing else. The window from the M9 preparations to the 17:35 reading is therefore about 25.9 h, not 6, and it spans both the period when those lines were still running and the period when they were not. It cannot date the onset of the failure, and no reading taken today could have.

What the 17:35 reading does establish, from the logged volumes alone:

  patrick M9 -- low 500 -> 270 mL, high 500 -> 420 mL. 230 and 80 mL drawn.
  plankton M9 -- low 500 -> 190 mL, high 500 -> 450 mL. 310 and 50 mL drawn.

Both units' M9 vials drew substantial volume across the window, so a total stall for the whole 25.9 h is excluded -- these vessels were dispensing for some of it. That is all it excludes. Because the window opens on 26 Aug, before the lines were re-seeded and before the reported failure, the draw is consistent with normal dilution followed by a stop at any point, and equally consistent with slow dilution throughout. Distinguishing those needed an intermediate reading that was never taken.

The reading is still worth having, and for a reason unrelated to INC-0009: all eight active reservoirs now carry a measured level from the same minute, the first time that has been true. Every rate tools/media.py reports from here is measured within one bottle rather than carried over or inferred, and the low-to-high ratio gives a delivered-dose estimate for all four groups at once. Take those rates from media.py rather than from this note: the arithmetic above is a difference of two logged volumes, not a rate, and the window it spans is not a period of uniform behaviour.

  In between -- growing but slowly, which is what M9 minimal medium can look like and would need OD from the rig to separate from a partial failure.

experiment_events.notes:
Physical relocation half of the 5 PM media switch (see the 8 accompanying media_switch events, EVT-00480..487, for the media-background change and transfer protocol on each line). Previous culture left each vial before the new culture arrived, per the operator. Mapping (old vial -> new sleeve): plankton-v03 3->11, plankton-v04 4->12, plankton-v05#2 5->13, plankton-v06#2 6->14, plankton-v11#3 11->3, plankton-v12#5 12->4, plankton-v13#3 13->5, plankton-v14#3 14->6. This is a genuine mutual/reciprocal exchange -- each of the 4 pairs trades sleeve positions with the other line in its pair.

Deliberately NOT using this event type's new_unit/new_vial relocation fields (registered 2026-09-01, ISSUE_002): tested empirically before this write and confirmed a hard 409 in both directions for a reciprocal pair (e.g. relocating plankton-v03 to vial 11 is refused while plankton-v11#3 still occupies it, and the reverse is refused symmetrically) -- a live two-line trade cannot be expressed as two sequential relocate calls, since each destination is held by the very line moving the other direction until that line has itself already moved. No culture ended as part of this switch (confirmed with the operator); termination+restart was considered and explicitly rejected as a workaround, since it would misrepresent these as new founder lines, losing lineage depth/continuity and resetting media_switch_count instead of incrementing it.

Consequence: this event does NOT update line.unit/line.vial for any of the 8 lines (no new_unit/new_vial supplied, so no relocation is auto-projected). GET /vials/plankton/{3,4,5,6,11,12,13,14} and each line's own unit/vial fields will keep reporting the OLD positions until a human updates them directly in evolution_log.json. Separately, media_switch_count also did not auto-increment on any of the 8 lines from the accompanying media_switch events (checked empirically on plankton-v03 after EVT-00480: stayed 0) -- that counter needs the same kind of manual bump.

Both gaps EVT-00488 flagged as needing a direct edit to evolution_log.json are now closed, using the vacate/relocate hardware_swap mechanism (ISSUE_002 follow-up) that became available after EVT-00488 was written. line.unit/vial: fixed via 16 new hardware_swap events (EVT-00505..512 vacate, EVT-00513..520 relocate), one vacate then one relocate per line, each vacate clearing a destination before the reciprocal line's relocate landed there -- confirmed via GET /vials/plankton/{3,4,5,6,11,12,13,14} and each line's own unit/vial fields, all matching the intended swap. Note: the vacate mechanism failed with a raw schema-validation 422 ("unit: None is not of type 'string'") on first attempt earlier today; a retry of the identical request shortly after succeeded, suggesting a schema fix landed on the server in between -- nothing was corrupted by the failed attempt (verified: no state change, no stray event). media_switch_count: found already at 1 on all 8 lines when checked just now, without any explicit fix from this session -- this was NOT something the vacate/relocate events touched, so it was apparently corrected independently, server-side, by someone or something else. EVT-00488 itself remains accurate as a record of what was known and done at the time; only its claim that these two fields would need a direct edit is superseded.

Seed-culture setup on 2026-09-09: eight seed cultures were initiated from Plankton 10, 9, 7, and 6. For each isolate, one culture was inoculated into LB at the highest PG concentration with observed growth (respectively 5, 4, 4, and 3 g/L PG) and a paired culture was transferred from the PG-free M9 condition into fresh M9. All eight seed cultures were placed in a 37 C shaker for later seeding work. Exact setup time was not reported.

LB-M9 gradient setup on 2026-09-09: Plankton 10 and Plankton 7 were used in reciprocal five-step twofold serial LB-to-M9 and M9-to-LB mixing gradients. Both media bases contained 3 g/L PG, held constant across all steps; only the LB:M9 proportion changed. Serial transfer also reduced cell concentration across the gradient. Where M9 material was limited, M9 was added to the corresponding low-LB culture. Cultures from concentrated stocks used 10 uL inoculum in the first column and were brought to 400 uL with fresh medium before growth. Plates were sealed with breathable membrane covers and incubated shaking at 37 C. Exact setup time was not reported.

Experimental phenotyping on 2026-09-09: eight 96-well plates held four replicates of each of 16 cultures across LB and M9 with 0, 1, 2, 3, 4, or 5 g/L PG. In LB, observed growth limits were Plankton 10 at 5 g/L PG; Plankton 9 at 4 g/L; Plankton 7 at 4 g/L; and Plankton 6 at 3 g/L. No PG-containing M9 condition showed growth; growth occurred only in 0 g/L PG M9. Microscopy found healthy, viable cells appearing consistent with E. coli. Exact observation time was not reported.

Reported plate phenotyping for Patrick cultures 9 and 10: cultures were tested under 3 g/L PG in reciprocal LB-M9 serial-mixing gradients across columns 1-6 and 7-12. The reported growth pattern was growth in all LB-containing endpoint/rich conditions (columns 1 and 8-12); growth in M9 at columns 7, 2, and 3; weaker growth at column 4; and no growth at column 5. The reported interpretation is that an LB-supplied component mitigates the toxicity observed when cultures are switched into 3 g/L PG M9. The verbal setup description gives internally conflicting medium labels for intermediate gradient columns, so exact LB:M9 proportions were not inferred from it. The date and time of the physical assay were not reported; this event timestamps the report.

controller.summary: Turbidostat on raw sensor values with a deterministic PG ramp layered on the pump action. Dilution fires when the raw sensor value falls to or below the per-vial setpoint. Each dilution is a two-step cycle: two 5 mL dispenses, each split between the low and high reservoirs. The controller keeps the vial's PG concentration as its own state variable and appends it to vialN_drugconc.txt on every step.
controller.ramp_rule: The concentration is raised by target_ramp only when all three hold: (1) the number of dilutions already seen at the current concentration is at least number_consecutive_intervals, (2) the current growth period is shorter than interval, and (3) the current growth period is shorter than the previous one divided by 0.93 — i.e. growth has not slowed by more than about 7%. Otherwise the ramp is 0 and the concentration is held, with pump volumes chosen to keep it flat rather than to stop dosing.
controller.safety_constraint: find_optimal_pump_volumes forbids the intermediate concentration after step 1 from exceeding c1 + target, so cells are transiently diluted and never spiked above their current exposure.

state_files.drug_concentration: vialN_drugconc.txt — time, concentration. The controller's own record of each vial's PG concentration through the run.
state_files.pump_log: vialN_pump_log.txt — time, duration, pump id (in1 = low, in2 = high).
state_files.od_raw: vialN_od_135_raw.txt — raw sensor values driving the dilution trigger.

parameters.setpoint: Raw sensor value at or below which a dilution fires. Per vial. NOT CAPTURED.
parameters.interval: Maximum growth period, in hours, that still counts toward a ramp. Per vial. NOT CAPTURED.
parameters.number_consecutive_intervals: Dilutions required at one concentration before a ramp. NOT CAPTURED.
parameters.initial_concentration: Starting vial PG concentration. Believed 0 for all lines.
parameters.low_concentration: PG in the low reservoir: 0 g/L until 2026-08-23T03:11, 0.5 g/L for LB after.
parameters.high_concentration: PG in the high reservoir: 5 g/L.
parameters.target_ramp: Concentration increment per successful ramp: 0.05 g/L.
parameters.volume: Vial working volume used in the concentration arithmetic. NOT CAPTURED — see design.pg_ramp.open_questions.
